ns a\n> different wait: a per-minute burst brake (`429`, retry in seconds), your\n> organization's daily generation quota (`429`,
resets at UTC midnight), and\n> MCPJam's own daily budget for the feature (`429` with\n> `details.code: \"platform_capacity\"`, re
sets at UTC midnight). All three carry\n> `Retry-After` — honor it rather than guessing. `details.canTopUp` is `false`\n> on every

one: buying credits does not lift them, so do not retry in a loop
> or switch identities to get around them.

**Swarms — runs*

* (`/projects/{projectId}/goals/{goalId}/runs`,
`.../goal-runs/...`) — launching a goal and reading what it produced:

| Endpoi

nt | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | That goal's runs, newest first |
| `POST .../goals/{goalId}/run
s` | **Launch.** Answers `202` — the fan-out has started, not finished. Send `Idempotency-Key`. Optional `expectedSponsored` is ho
w many conversations you expect MCPJam to sponsor; a different actual split is a `409` (`details.code: swarm_funding_changed`) and
nothing is created. The response can report `funding` (`sponsored`, `credits`, `total`) |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}` | The fu
ll run: counts, per-target breakdown, per-session `attempts` |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions` | The chat sessions the run
produced (summaries, not transcripts) |\n| `POST .../goal-runs/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempotent — a second cancel is `200

` with `alreadyCanceled: true`, not a `409` |

Three things worth knowing before you write the client:

* **Always send `Idemp
otency-Key` on a launch.** It spends model credits, so a\n retry of a dropped response must not run the goal twice. Replaying a k
ey\n returns the original run with `deduped: true` and starts no second runner —\n and consumes no quota. Omitting the header is
read as a request that declined\n to identify itself, and gets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canceled` before reporting a
failure.** A stopped run carries\n `status: \"failed\"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than\n a status of
its own. `stale: true` is the third case: the runner went silent\n and the watchdog settled the run.\n* **`targetId`, not `hostId
`, identifies a target.** Two environments can\n resolve to the same host with different servers, so a run can hold two\n target

s that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Launching **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`
> sessions. Two d
ifferent `429`s can come back — the per-minute burst brake\n> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap (resets at UTC m

idnight).
> Both normally carry `Retry-After`; back off on your own when one does not.

**Swarms — insights** — what a run reve
aled. Read these in order of cost: the\nroll-up and the scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings registry\naggregates th

em, and swarm run insights run a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals-overview` | Project roll-up: r
ecent runs, goal-completion rates, repeat failures, trend |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's deterministic rub
ric result. No model, no spend |\n| `GET .../goal-findings` | Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swarm runs |\n| `POST ...
/goal-findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Hide a finding |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide it |\n| `GET ..
./swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Poll a swarm run's generated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |\n| `POST .../swarm-runs/{swa
rmRunId}/insights` | Request them. `202` — scheduled, not done |\n| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Cancel a gener

ation still `pending` |

Two arithmetic traps worth naming, because both produce numbers that look
plausible and are wrong:
* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, never by the session total.** Three failures\n out of four graded sessions, in a run that attempt

ed forty, is 75% — not
 7.5%.
* **`failedGradingCount` is not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a
 regression, and foldin

g the two together makes one look like the other.

And one modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecycle —
`new | recurri
ng | regressed | resolved`. `dismissed` is *not* one of them.\nDismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a finding can be both

recurring
and dismissed, and hiding one never claims it stopped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swarm run insights c
onsumes **no credits** — the model cost is on\n> MCPJam. It still counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts\n> REQU
ESTS and is **shared** with eval-run and user-testing insights, so a\n> request here takes one from there too. Poll the `GET` rath

er than
> re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice.
>
> Three refusals, three different meanings: a short
`429` is the per-minute\n> brake (wait seconds), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `Retry-After`, when
present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403` means\n> the feature is not available to your organization — waiting will never help

.

**User testing** (`/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/study`,
`.../studies/...`) — publishing an environment
for real visitors, reading what\nthey did, and controlling who can reach it. A **study** is a published\nenvironment: one per env

ironment, addressed by its own id once it exists.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `PUT .../environments/{environmentI
d}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent — republishing returns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |\n
| `DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when ther
e was nothing published |\n| `PATCH .../studies/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}
/sessions` | What visitors did: one row per session, with feedback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/ses
sions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcript, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-ex
ecution` | The spend dial for anonymous visitors: daily credits, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rot
ate-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No body — the new secret is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | I
nvite someone (or change their role) on an `invited_only` study |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Re
move someone. Their grant is revoked, ending their live sessions |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a d

ifferent environment in the same project |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who already used it.**
It stops the\n> old URL from granting NEW access; the grants already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the single most impo
rtant thing to know here, because rotation\n> is what you reach for when a link leaks — and on its own it does not undo the\n> lea
k. Rotate *and* remove the members you did not intend to have.\n>\n> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessions rather th
an waiting for\n> expiry: unpublishing, tightening `mode`, and removing a member. Those bump\n> the study's `accessVersion`, and a
session minted under an older version\n> stops working. None of them reverse by calling the opposite — a re-invited\n> member get

s a new session, not their old one.
>
> Read `accessVersion` off the publish and rebind responses. The update and
> rotate resp

onses do not carry it.

**User testing — what visitors did** — the analytics reads, and the model pass
over them. Read these in

cost order: metrics, usage and signals are
deterministic and free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it do
es |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` sp
lits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions used. **C
heck `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the current windo
w — and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed o
nes included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/windows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, w
